cohort: 215,993 nulliparous women who delivered single infants in British Columbia from 1999 to 2011, including 9,152 First Nations mothers.
finding: Compared to the general population, First Nations mothers in British Columbia were less likely to receive certain obstetric care services aligned with best practice guidelines, such as early ultrasonography and a sufficient number of antenatal care visits, and also had a lower utilization of obstetric interventions.
